Third category selection-based navigation/locomotion. Allows users focus on where to go rather than how to. Previous techniques specify how by steering/looking/performing work; selection-based select destination.

Target selection: user selects destination/target, virtual viewpoint changes, feels moved. Common technique teleportation: instantly moving from current to target. Map dragging fix location instantly move. Jumper technique in cave-type systems: select target, viewpoint changes instant travel.
Route planning: selection-based, not only end selected; more granular control over travel than teleportation/target-based where endpoint selected and instant move. Select route to target, multiple routes, user selects route, while moving through route different viewpoint changes implemented so user feels moving along path. Slightly more natural movement than target-based teleportation.
Final category manipulation-based locomotion. Works by manipulating user's position, orientation, or scale using gestures that control virtual viewpoint or virtual world. Earlier discussed go-go, homer, world in miniature. Combination implement. Example world in miniature: move/manipulate objects, corresponding change in viewpoint as if user moving. Already discussed, refer previous lectures. End discussion on locomotion techniques.
